note:
Yeomons book on stat. mech. of phase transitions (ch. 8) has some critical insight that I don't fully understand. Summary of what (I think) I do understand:
* free energy looks to be the main function under question
* various operations on free energy provide quantities people care about (specific heat is second derivative of free energy rel. some parameter @ some point, magnetization, correlation length, etc.)
* free energy and partition function might be interchangeable with some simple substitution (?) (often partition function is said to be the main function of interest)
* renormization group operations (of free energy) at criticial points are often/sometimes characterized by attractive or repulsive fixed points
* linearizing motion around fixed points gives a matrx representation
* change variables/standardize variables to get exponents of the (two) eigenvalues
* relate exponents to each of the quantities of interest (spec. heat, magnetization, etc.)
* if conformally invariant, this produces extra restrictions on relation between the (two) eigenvalues, leading to simple rational relations (??)
* conformal invariance comes from some conservation law (I believe), in this case scale invariance (at the critical point)
* under some conditions, which I don't really understand (Virasoro algebra, Kac table, minimal model), confomal invariance and the extra restriction of the model (ising, q-potts, etc.) lead to rational relations between the two eigenvalues, leading to simple rational relations between critical exponents of interest.
